description.text: AI-written synthesis of the cited official pages, prepared by the collecting assistant: Formerly known as Alchemist Accelerator, Alchemist now explicitly describes itself as an early-stage venture firm rather than an accelerator. It backs deeply technical enterprise teams at pre-seed and seed, with checks ranging from $60,000 to $1 million depending on the company and program. Its founder experience includes a matched equity-aligned Partner, commercialization and fundraising support, a mentor network, and an ongoing founder community. The main founder experience has no set program length and does not require moving to San Francisco. Regional Chicago and Japan programs still have set calendars; their terms should not be treated as a uniform Alchemist deal. The current official pages checked do not establish a single fixed equity percentage, investment instrument, or next main-program cohort deadline.

targetApplicants.text: AI-written synthesis of the cited official pages, prepared by the collecting assistant: Alchemist targets deeply technical researchers, engineers, and domain experts who are ready to commercialize and sell to enterprise customers. It invests at pre-seed and seed, is sector agnostic, and identifies AI and deep tech as major focus areas. The FAQ includes B2B and B2B2C companies, hardware and software, and customers ranging from SMBs to Fortune 500 businesses. Solo founders may apply, although Alchemist describes a higher bar and says most portfolio companies start with two or three committed co-founders. It invests outside the United States and says its structure works with the founder's country of incorporation. A warm introduction is not required: the public founder form goes directly to the investment team.

sources.title: Alchemist official press kit — primary mark asset
Alchemist FAQ — current name, venture-firm positioning, and no fixed duration
sources.quote:
Alchemist no longer considers itself an accelerator. We are an early-stage venture firm, and our focus is guiding deeply technical teams to enterprise traction. We do so through our Founder experience, a proven commercialization method that does not run on a set program length. We support our portfolio companies for as long as they are building toward a venture-scale outcome.

[…]

Alchemist no longer calls itself Alchemist Accelerator. We now do business as Alchemist, at alchemist.vc. We are the same firm and the same team that founders have known since 2012, and our legal entity is still Alchemist Accelerator, LLC. Links to alchemistaccelerator.com bring you here.

[…]

Our partners in Chicago and Japan still run programs on a set calendar with a start date and a showcase.

sources.title: Alchemist FAQ — current investment range, stages, and sector policy
sources.quote:
What stage does Alchemist invest in?

Pre-seed and seed. We back founders who are ready to commercialize and get in front of enterprise customers now.

How much does Alchemist invest?

Our check size ranges from $60,000 to $1 million, depending on the company and the program.

[…]

We are sector agnostic. Our portfolio spans AI, deep tech, data and analytics, developer tools, IoT, health, sales and marketing, manufacturing, financial services and more. AI is our largest field, and we have a strong focus in deep tech, backing companies across quantum computing, energy, robotics, sensing, drones, biotech, climate, semiconductors, aerospace and defense.

sources.title: Alchemist FAQ — enterprise teams, solo founders, and global incorporation
sources.quote:
We back B2B businesses whose sale is complex and needs a method behind it. That includes:

B2B and B2B2C
Both hardware and software
Buyers of all sizes, from SMB to Fortune 500
License, SaaS or usage-based models

[…]

We back deeply technical researchers, engineers and domain experts building the next generation of enterprise infrastructure and technology.

[…]

Does Alchemist back solo founders?

Yes, though it is a higher bar for solo founders, because it is harder to execute before you have assembled a founding team. Most Alchemist companies start with two or three committed co-founders with complementary skills.

Does Alchemist invest outside the United States?

Yes. Our founders come from 60+ countries across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, and our investment structure works with your country of incorporation.

sources.title: Alchemist FAQ — founder support and Partner equity alignment
sources.quote:
The Alchemist founder experience is everything a founder gets from Alchemist once we invest: hands-on commercialization and fundraising support, our global network, and a community of founders that stays with you. Every founder we back gets it for as long as they are building toward a venture-scale outcome.

[…]

Alchemist assigns part of its equity to Partners, so their incentives are aligned with yours. There are no advisor shares to negotiate and no extra line on your cap table.

sources.title: Alchemist FAQ — San Francisco home and optional office access
sources.quote:
Where is Alchemist based?

Our home is San Francisco. We also run programs in Chicago with the Polsky Center at the University of Chicago, in Doha with QRDI Council, and in Tokyo. Our portfolio spans founders from 60+ countries.

[…]

Do I need to move to San Francisco?

No. You can build from anywhere. Our San Francisco office is yours when you need it. If you are based in Silicon Valley, or move here, you can get regular access to a desk for six months. Otherwise, you are always welcome to drop in whenever you are in Silicon Valley.

sources.title: Alchemist FAQ — public founder form and no warm introduction requirement
sources.quote:
How do I pitch Alchemist?

Share your company through our founder form. It goes straight to our investment team.

[…]

Do I need a warm introduction?

No. Our founder form goes straight to our investment team, so you can reach us directly.
